If g is twice continuously real-differentiable locally at the scalar point s, then both ∇f(x) = (2g′(s))(x − a) and Δf(x) = 4s g″(s) + 2(dimℝ E)g′(s). Here g′ is the ordinary real derivative, g″ is the derivative of g′, ∇ is the Riesz representative of the actual Fréchet derivative, and Δ is the orthonormal trace of the actual second Fréchet derivative. The dimension is interpreted as a real scalar in the displayed formula. The conclusions hold at the specified point x, including x = a; no positive-dimension, nonzero-distance, positive-radius, or global C² assumption is imposed.
